why: the bounded blocking loop: call `spin_once(poll_ms)` until `duration_ms` of wall clock has elapsed, WAITING for new work the whole time. rclcpp has no verb with that meaning -- `spin_some(max_duration)` and `spin_all(max_duration)` both return as soon as the ready set drains. Issue 0338 considered naming this `spin_some(max_duration)` and deliberately chose `spin_for`, because the semantics are not rclcpp's; the same issue moved `spin()` TO rclcpp's meaning (blocks until this executor is shut down) and left the old bounded two-argument `spin` as a one-release `[[deprecated]]` alias.
